newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Venetian separatists could get up to 30 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Italy Venetian separatists could get up to 30 yrs.

text.p: Eight Italians who took over the bell tower in St Mark's Square in Venice in a separatist protest will go on trial next week and could face 30 years in jail if convicted, judicial sources said on Tuesday.

The sources said the eight would stand summary trial from May 21 charged with kidnapping for subversive ends after they hijacked a ferry to take them and a home-made armoured vehicle to the square early last Friday.
The offence carries a prison sentence of 25 to 30 years on conviction, according to Italy's penal code.
Friday's siege was ended peacefully after five hours when police scaled the bell tower and arrested the separatists who claimed to represent the "Venetian Liberation Army".
Police later found a sub-machinegun which prosecutors allege the separatists had used to threaten the ferry pilot.
One of the eight, Flavio Contin, told Corriere della Sera newspaper in an interview from jail that the group had intended only to create publicity.

"We didn't want to hurt anyone. We wouldn't have been capable. We just wanted to make a symbolic gesture. We wanted to get on radio and television, everywhere. That was our objective," Contin was quoted as saying.
"We only expected to go to jail for a few days," he added.
Monday was the 200th anniversary of the fall of the Venetian Republic which was for centuries an independent power with control stretching down the Adriatic and into the Middle East.
Known as the "Most Serene Republic", it fell on May 12, 1797, when French forces of Napoleon Bonaparte entered the city.
